macro.title: RBI hikes repo rate to 5.50%
macro.summary: The MPC voted unanimously to raise the policy repo rate by 25 bps to 5.50% (SDF 5.25%, MSF 5.75%) to contain inflation that has breached the upper tolerance band.
macro.impact: Banking & NBFCs: margin pass-through helps lenders with sticky deposit costs; near-term pressure on rate-sensitive sectors — real estate, auto, infrastructure, and long-duration growth stocks.

macro.title: CPI inflation jumps to 6.09% in October
macro.summary: Retail CPI rose to 6.09% from 5.54%, the 12th consecutive monthly increase, breaching the RBI’s 6% upper tolerance band. Food and fuel were the main drivers.
macro.impact: High inflation limits RBI’s room for rate cuts and keeps borrowing costs elevated. Hits consumer discretionary and input-heavy manufacturers; favours firms with strong pricing power.

macro.title: Fed holds rates at 3.75%–4.00%
macro.summary: The FOMC kept the federal funds target range unchanged at 3.75%–4.00% after a 25 bps hike in September. Markets price a hold or at most one cut in December.
macro.impact: A higher-for-longer US rate keeps the rate differential in favour of the dollar, pressuring the rupee and limiting FII risk appetite. A dovish pivot would be a positive catalyst for Indian equities.

macro.title: Next-Gen GST reforms roll out from Nov 1
macro.summary: GST shifts to a "Trust First, Verify Later" regime with phased compliance reforms, faster refunds, higher prosecution threshold (₹1 Cr → ₹5 Cr) and lower penalties. Gross GST collections grew 11.6% YoY to ~₹12.46 lakh crore in H1.
macro.impact: Easier compliance and faster refunds ease working capital for MSMEs and manufacturers. Boosts e-commerce, logistics, FMCG and formal-sector consumption.

macro.title: FIIs pour ~₹66,300 Cr into equities in November
macro.summary: Foreign investors net bought roughly ₹66,300 crore in the first seven sessions of November (full-month net ~₹1.01 lakh crore), driving benchmarks to nine-month highs. The rupee strengthened above 92.67/USD.
macro.impact: Strong FII flows benefit large-cap, high-liquidity names and banking/IT heavyweights. A reversal would hit the same segments first. Rupee strength helps importers and hurts exporters’ rupee realisations.
